largest_measured_cost_component.within_propagation: times_fixpoint + _t + addresses_fixpoint + _a own time = 38.3% of profiled time; dict.get (14.3%) and len (3.2%) are called mainly from the same accessors

mechanism: Incremental (worklist) revision in Propagation.times_fixpoint and Propagation.addresses_fixpoint. The frozen code re-sweeps EVERY edge/pair after any deletion, and a child call starts from a parent domain that is already a fixpoint, so at least one full sweep per child re-checks edges that cannot fire. The variant keeps a queue of edges (pairs) incident to operations (values) whose domain changed, starting from the assigned decision for a child call and from every edge at the root; the engine-capacity rule is applied after each edge quiescence exactly as before. Accessor calls are replaced by one merged lookup table. All rules are deletion-only and monotone, so the greatest fixpoint (or the proof of inconsistency) is unique: surviving domains, prunes, children and bounds are unchanged; only the ORDER and grouping of emitted certificates may change.

identical pruning decisions and child domains on exhaustive fixtures
every emitted certificate still replays as sound
